'''Richard H. Price''' (born March 1, 1943) is an American [[physicist]] specializing in [[general relativity]]. He is known for Price’s theorem and contributions to [[black hole]] perturbation theory.

== Early life and education ==
Price graduated from [[Stuyvesant High School]] in 1960, and went on to earn a dual degree in physics and engineering from [[Cornell University]] in 1965. He earned his PhD in 1971 from [[Caltech]] under the supervision of [[Kip Thorne]].<ref name="URI"/>

== Career ==
Price spent his career from 1971 to 2004 at the [[University of Utah]], where he holds the title of emeritus professor.<ref>[http://www.physics.utah.edu/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=578&catid=173 Richard Price Emeritus Professor] University of Utah, Retrieved 23 September 2017</ref> In 2004, he joined the [[Center for Gravitational Wave Astronomy]] at the [[University of Texas at Brownsville]]. As of 2015, he became senior lecturer in physics at [[MIT]]. He is also on the adjunct faculty at the [[University of Massachusetts Dartmouth]].<ref>[http://www.umassd.edu/engineering/phy/people/facultyandstaff/richardprice/ UMass Dartmouth faculty page] Retrieved 23 September 2017</ref>

In 2017, Price became the editor of the ''[[American Journal of Physics]]''.<ref name="editor">{{cite web|last1=Wolfe|first1=David|title=Richard Price to Become Next Editor of American Journal of Physics|url=https://www.aapt.org/aboutaapt/pressreleases/Richard_Price_to_Become_Next_Editor_of_American_Journal_of_Physics.cfm|website=American Association of Physics Teachers|accessdate=20 July 2017|language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
=== Price’s theorem ===
Price is probably best known for a 1972 theorem that is usually informally stated as follows: ''any inhomogeneities in the spacetime geometry outside a black hole will be radiated away''.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Price
|first=Richard H.
|title=Nonspherical Perturbations of Relativistic Gravitational Collapse. I. Scalar and Gravitational Perturbations
|journal=Physical Review D|volume=5
|issue=10|pages=2419–2438
|date=1972|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.5.2419
|url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.23242}}</ref>
(Any such inhomogeneities can be quantified as nonzero higher [[multipole moment]]s.) Price's theorem explains how the [[no hair theorem]] is enforced.

=== Numerical relativity ===
Price also made pioneering numerical simulations which established (nonrigorously) a precise scenario for the emission of gravitational radiation during the merger of two compact objects (such as two [[black hole]]s).<ref>{{cite journal |last=Price |first=Richard H. |last2=Bachhar |first2=Ritesh |last3=Khanna |first3=Gaurav |title=Binary black hole coalescence phenomenology from numerical relativity |journal=Physical Review D |volume=113 |issue=4 |year=2026 |doi=10.1103/kk1h-rh4h|arxiv=2312.15885 }}</ref> Subsequent work has largely confirmed the scenario which was first developed in his work. These simulations have provided a major impetus for the development of [[gravitational wave]] detectors such as [[LIGO]].<ref>{{cite journal
|last=Gleiser|first=Reinaldo J.|author2=Nicasio, Carlos O.
|author3=Price, Richard H.|author4=Pullin, Jorge
|title=Gravitational radiation from Schwarzschild black holes: The second-order perturbation formalism
|journal=Physics Reports|volume=325
|pages=41–81|year=2000
|doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(99)00048-4|url=https://the-center-of-gravity.com/documents/270/Francisco_Duque_PhD_2023.pdf}}</ref> He has also produced relativity visualizations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gravitational Radiation Visualizations |url=https://web.mit.edu/viz/gravrad/visualizations/theTheory/theTheory.htm |website=MIT Gravitation Visualizations |access-date=28 May 2026}}</ref>

== Teaching and honors ==
Price has done much in development of pedagogical techniques in physics at the undergraduate, graduate, and postdoc levels;<ref>{{cite web |title=Richard Price to Become Next Editor of American Journal of Physics|url=https://aapt.org/aboutaapt/pressreleases/Richard_Price_to_Become_Next_Editor_of_American_Journal_of_Physics.cfm |website=AAPT |date=20 October 2016 |access-date=29 May 2026}}</ref> a significant portion at the [[University of Utah]] in [[Salt Lake City]], Utah.<ref name="URI"<ref>{{cite web |title=Richard H. Price |url=https://web.uri.edu/gravity/meet/richard-h-price/ |website=URI Gravity Group |access-date=28 May 2026}}</ref>

Price is the coauthor of three well known books in [[general relativity]]. 
He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="editor"/>
